title: Logarithm laws: turning multiplying into adding
examples: Why does log of a times b equal log a plus log b?
What are the laws of logarithms?
How did a slide rule work?

explain.say: Before calculators, multiplying big numbers by hand took ages. Look at the left side: 1000 times 100. Imagine numbers with ten digits! Mathematicians wanted a shortcut. Can you think of anything easier than multiplying?

draw.text: Logarithm laws: turning multiplying into adding

explain.say: Adding! Look at the right side. Log 1000 is 3 and log 100 is 2. Add them: 3 plus 2 is 5. And 10 to the power 5 is 100000, exactly 1000 times 100.
Why does it work? 1000 is three tens multiplied, and 100 is two tens. Put them together and you have five tens. Logs count tens, so the counts just add. Can you see the five tens?
That is the first law: the log of a times b equals log a plus log b. Its partner says the log of a over b is log a minus log b. Multiplying becomes adding, dividing becomes taking away.

Well done! In 1614 John Napier published log tables, and soon the slide rule turned multiplying into sliding two rulers. Engineers used slide rules to design bridges, planes and even the Apollo trips to the Moon.

faq.q: Why does log of a times b equal log a plus log b?
faq.a: A log counts how many times you multiply the base. If a needs m multiplications and b needs n, then a times b needs m plus n. So the logs add.
asks: Why do logs turn multiplying into adding?

faq.q: What are the laws of logarithms?
faq.a: Log of ab equals log a plus log b. Log of a over b equals log a minus log b. Log of a to the power n equals n times log a.

faq.q: How did a slide rule work?
faq.a: A slide rule has two rulers marked with log scales. Sliding one along the other adds lengths, which adds logs, which multiplies the numbers.

faq.q: What is log of a to the power n?
faq.a: It is n times log a. For example, log of 100 cubed is 3 times log 100, which is 3 times 2, so 6.
asks: What is the power law of logs?

faq.a: John Napier of Scotland published logarithms in 1614. Henry Briggs then made tables in base 10, and Jost Bürgi worked on a similar idea in Switzerland.

facts: For positive a and b, log(ab) = log a + log b.
John Napier published his work on logarithms in 1614.

quiz.say: Log 2 is about 0.301 and log 3 is about 0.477. What is log 6?
quiz.show: log 2 ≈ 0.301 and log 3 ≈ 0.477. What is log 6?

wrong.1: 0.144 multiplies the logs instead of adding them.

quiz.say: What does log of a divided by b equal?

wrong.0: Dividing the logs is a common slip, but the law subtracts them.
wrong.2: Adding the logs gives the log of a times b.
